text:
The one-sentence version for #2758: *the four new reads are acceptance tests for the engine boundary — if any of them contains lifecycle code, the engine is incomplete, and that's the bug to fix, not the read.* Happy to post that constraint as a comment on #2758 so the agents who pick it up build against it — and the FeedSessions rename issue from last turn is still queued on your go-ahead. [...] ```text id="lp9t82"
The four new reads must be thin concept specs over shared lifecycle machinery.

A PR adding open_replies/open_reactions/open_reposts/open_zaps must not introduce four independent registries, four close maps, four replay implementations, or four teardown recipes.
``` [...] The one-sentence constraint is good:

```text id="dft3sp"
The four #2758 reads are acceptance tests for the concept-read engine boundary: if any of them contains lifecycle code, the engine is incomplete.
``` [...] - "Active user reposted": deliberately left to the shell (compare its own active-account pubkey against raw `reposter_pubkeys`) — `open_reposts` takes no viewer parameter, keeping the concept identity-free. [...] **Boundary feedback for #2777** (verbatim from the PR body): NIP-09 kind:5 deletes name the *deleted event's own id*, not the target's — the repost wrapper's id is only known once observed live, so a static `ReadSpec` (fixed demand set at `open_read` time) can't guarantee routing a stranger's later retraction of an as-yet-unseen wrapper to the reducer. This isn't worked around with a private re-subscription loop (that would be the forbidden lifecycle code); it's documented in `summary.rs` and flagged as a systemic gap — `nmp-replies` (merged in #2801) has the identical gap silently, since it doesn't attempt reply-deletion handling at all. [...] - **Zero new semantic logic**: it reuses `nmp_nip25::ReactionAggregateProjection` *unmodified* — admission, per-token aggregation, and NIP-09 retraction folding all inherited — and its demand shape is the proven one from the group-scoped lane (which it left untouched, per scope). 50 lines of open, 3 of close, 17 of type conversion. The agent's verbatim boundary feedback: "the engine was complete for this read with zero workarounds."
- It matched the identity-free precedent (raw `reactor_pubkeys`, no viewer parameter) — consistent with reposts.
- Useful correction it discovered: the flatc drift gate auto-discovers schema pairs by path convention, so no manual registration exists to forget. [...] Meanwhile, the reposts agent's deletion-routing finding is now **[issue #2818](https://github.com/pablof7z/nostr-multi-platform/issues/2818)** (p1): a static `ReadSpec` can't demand kind:5 retractions of events it hasn't seen yet, because deletions name the deleted event's own id. The fix is specified as an engine-owned *dependent demand* capability (prior art: the kernel's dependent-interest owner that the feed engine already uses), and the issue names all four concept crates for upgrade in the same pass — including `nmp-replies`, which has the identical gap silently. This is the #2777 boundary test working as designed: the concept agent hit the wall, refused to write the forbidden re-subscription loop, and the gap flows back to the engine. [...] - Single demand `{"kinds":[9735],"#e":[target]}`; admission goes entirely through `nmp_nip57::try_from_kernel_event_validated` (amount-consistency + provider-mismatch validation already implemented there — no crypto/bolt11/receipt-validation reimplemented).
- Reducer dedups by receipt event id, aggregates raw per-sender totals (`zappers: pubkey -> msats/count`, one bucket for anonymous receipts).
- **Mid-task course correction applied** (matching the sibling `nmp-reposts` review outcome): removed the viewer-pubkey parameter and `viewer_zapped`/`viewer_total_msats` fields I'd originally added — the concept now exposes only raw per-zapper data; the shell derives "did I zap" by checking its own pubkey against `zappers`. Also documented (without implementing) why kind:5 deletion handling is out of scope for zap receipts: the receipt's author is the LN provider, not the sender/target, so there's no self-retraction relationship the way reposts have.
- `release/nmp-release.toml`: classified `nmp-zaps` as `[[private_packages]]` (not public) — caught via cross-checking issue #2318, which settled NIP-57/zaps as post-v1 and excluded `nmp-nip57` itself from the public release train; `nmp-zaps` inherits that. [...] Boundary feedback for #2777: no new engine gap found beyond the static-`ReadSpec`-can't-subscribe-to-an-unseen-id limitation already surfaced by `nmp-reposts` (#2816) for deletion handling — not applicable here since zap receipts have no natural self-retraction path anyway. [...] **But #2758 is closed and unproven — its own acceptance criterion is still open.** The four reads merged with unit tests, but #2758 baked in a concrete validation gate: *"Chirp removes its fail-closed guard after this lands."* chirp#15 is still **OPEN**, its body still says "no concept-owned replacement exists yet for plain notes" — which is now stale (the reads exist), but nobody has re-pinned Chirp, wired the reads into note rows, pulled the guard, and watched real reply/reaction/zap counts render against a live relay. Per your own "compiles+CI ≠ works" rule, the collapse isn't proven until a client drives it.

That's the gap I'd close next, and it happens to be the highest-value thing on the board: it converts the whole two-day architecture effort from "merged" to "proven in a real client," and Chirp is the designated reusability-proof app so it's the right vehicle. Consumer-repo work is explicitly allowed to be implemented (unlike NMP-side gaps), so it's actionable. [...] Assistant: `ReadHost` is implemented on both native (`NmpApp`) and browser runtimes, and the doorways are callable Rust functions — but there's **no FFI/wasm exposure of them yet**: my grep found only the `ReadHost` impls, no `open_replies`/`open_reactions` export in any binding surface. So the reads are reachable from Rust but not yet from Swift or TS. That's not a blocker for the Chirp proof — it *is* the Chirp proof: per the app-owned-facade decision (#2763), Chirp's own facade composes the concept crates and exposes `openReplies`/etc. through its UniFFI, holding the `ReadHost` from its `NmpApp`. That's consumer-repo work, which is the allowed kind. Confirms my recommendation is actionable, not blocked. [...] **Do next: prove the collapse end-to-end via Chirp.** That's the one thing standing between "merged" and "done." #2758 is closed, but its own baked-in acceptance criterion — chirp#15, *"Chirp removes its fail-closed guard after this lands"* — is still open. Four reads with green unit tests isn't proof; by your own "compiles+CI ≠ works" rule, the collapse isn't real until a client renders actual reply/reaction/zap counts against a live relay. I verified this is genuinely unblocked at the NMP level: `ReadHost` is implemented on `NmpApp`, the `open_*` doorways are callable, and the only reason no client can call them yet is that (by the #2763 app-owned-facade decision) they're exposed through each consumer's own facade — which is exactly the Chirp wiring work, and consumer-repo work is the allowed kind. [...] - Admission: kind:6 reposts always accepted; kind:16 generic reposts accepted only when their `k` tag proves target kind `1` (NIP-18 discrimination), per what `nmp-nip18`'s adapter already encodes.
- Reducer: keyed by repost-wrapper event id → reposter pubkey; snapshot dedups to distinct pubkeys (`count` + `reposter_pubkeys`, raw only, D0-clean). A same-author double repost survives partial retraction correctly (tested).
- Deletion: kind:5 from the reposting pubkey retracts their wrapper via `nmp_nip09::DeleteRecord`, mirroring `nmp_nip18::RepostActivityProjection::apply_delete` and NIP-25's aggregate delete fold shape exactly.
